notes.title: Character Introduction: Lord of the Flies
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/07fd9a3bef003d3238441c625ad41ad8970554b0.png[/img]
In chapter 3, “Lord of the Flies,” you get to meet a criminal who lives two lives: unknown to all, he's a skilled hacker, but notoriously, he is a popular exposé-type V-avatar, using the alias “Lord of the Flies."

He hacks into  security cameras and drones throughout Tokyo to spy on politicians and people with significant high profiles to get the dirt on them. Despite over 3 million subscribers on his account where he spreads their scandals all over the internet, he's managed to retain his anonymity so far, but his enemies aren't few; the bounty on his head exceeds 100 million yen.

Beneath the facade of his v-avatar, he is secretly researching a severe corruption case related to a public works project. What is his real objective for risking his own life to expose all the black rumors that surround him? While the police and bounty hunters from around the world are in pursuit of him, the Lord of the Flies operates his rumble gear remotely, leading a swarm of drones to face Officer Sakuragi! What will become of her?

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: Spring has come!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/f48b444ad734faea7e8034b12d7a7aaef8854fc5.png[/img]
I started drawing this in March, but by the time I was done all the cherry blossoms had already fallen……

Destruction is a big part of the game, so now we're working on making tons of background graphics and destroyable objects. We're eager to show you all what it looks like in action, so we're working on it everyday.

As the weather is starting to get warm, things are heating up in development too! Hope you look forward to it!

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: Viper the Chivalrous
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/5cb9d612dc88a2ce5cf8a8156f8977ce4477bb23.png[/img]
An independent AI created by the late professor Eleanor Stoneman, who was known for her unconventional approach to AI research. Created with "Beliefs from Lore" embedded in its core, Viper grew into a character with an obsession for aesthetics. Its principles and behaviour center around one rule: To be cool. Viper believes itself to be the last hero left in this mad world.

Using stolen Rumble Gear to save the weak and eat the rich, Viper targets corrupt politicians and mobs to steal from, with the purpose to distribute wealth to the poor and charitable organizations.

Surprisingly, Viper is quite aware that its actions and values are too good to be true, and that good and bad can never be black and white. Nevertheless, this does not sway Viper, because "living up to one's own beliefs is the coolest thing to do."

In the 2nd episode, “The Great Outcast,” Officer Sakuragi comes in contact with Viper on an illegal gambling boat. Will Viper be her friend or foe……?

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: Rumble Gear
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/923a7f4ce71776e154a10119b6b6b42ba286ae5f.png[/img]
"Rumble Gear" is the term used to call the two-legged exoskeletons in Scramble Vice. 

Originally, they were manufactured as robot suits to help foot soldiers seize control of war zones , but during the 21st century, after a global treaty restricted use of middle to long-range missiles, they gained wider recognition for military use because of their high mobility, ability to carry heavy weapons and short-range guided missiles.

The world has been relatively calm after the Northern Conflict, which lasted 5 years…… Yet big corporations in the robotics industry are thriving, and older generation exoskeletons are now either discarded, or traded on the black market to be used by terrorists.

With time, pilots coined the term "Rumble Gear," partly sardonically, knowing that even the most advanced technology is ultimately nothing more than a disposable tool used for fighting.

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: Wingmen
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/138c79fee19740c0eae8744e391bbb07e0eeb4b0.png[/img]
Scramble Vice is a single player action game, but to create the effect of being on a team, we're creating a "Wingman" system where support characters may come and help. Each team member of the 9th unit will ride a wingman machine with its own unique characteristics.

Allow me to introduce a few.

"Johnny"
Used by the unit leader "Jōtarō Jingūji". It specializes in rescue operations in hazardous situations. Its strength lies in its capability to move through rough footing, making it the perfect companion to Sakuragi after she's destroyed the roads during her missions. It's a reliable machine, but may fall short in speed and is not as suitable for combat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/6671203f8ea3476c2aaba340967b3d6746ddc5a7.png[/img]

"Betty"
The unit used by "Professor", a defiant old man who originally worked for Public Security. It has large rocket thrusters installed in lieu of legs, allowing it to elevate itself to reach high areas easily. However, its airborne functions consume a lot of fuel, so it rarely gets called on site. Also, because of its thrusters, it cannot have large artillery installed for stability reasons. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/936e68c674e28af98cb881a3464e2376c8ec0ad0.png[/img]

As you can see, every machine of the 9th mobility unit has its own strengths and weaknesses. We hope that's something you'll look forward to!

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: Wanted Criminals
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/152b22cff08d3219bc068cb53962e87461f2681b.png[/img]
Our previous game ”Shinobi non Grata" was created to work like an arcade game, and we were quite particular about it. It paid off, and we were able to make the gameplay fast-paced the way a ninja game should be. For "Scramble Vice" we're trying to focus on destruction instead of speed as the element of fun.

There are several named "Wanted Criminals" in Scramble Vice that have absolutely nothing to do with the 12 chapter main story. Finding them is a part of the fun. Why are they wanted? What kind of machines do they ride, and how do they fight?

I'll tell you a little bit about one such criminal, dubbed "Snake Eyes".
He owns an illegal casino on a ship, is a gambler himself, and a veteran pilot that fought in the Northern War. He wears an exoskeleton and finds excitement in betting his life on each fight he gets himself into, survival being his ultimate prize.

Having lost his eyes in a previous fight, he currently wears AI prosthetics that have the pupils colored red. Hence his name, Snake Eyes, which is a gambling term meaning a roll of two 1s on a pair of six-sided dice. He's a wanted criminal for his illegal gambling business and several murder charges.

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: The music of Scramble Vice
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/facb0496d9d71695c0780cb5d11789c5d4bd8de9.png[/img]

Music played a big part in our decision to create a 90's anime styled game in 2024. While creating our current PV, we tried various types of music to figure out what would work best. It came as no surprise, however, that retro jazz fusion suited the game the most. Once that was decided, it also helped other areas of the game's design to take shape.

When I was a kid, I used to watch the reruns of "Lupin the 3rd" and "Space Adventure COBRA" (which my parents tried forbid me to watch) every week, and I still love both animations to this day. I watched "Cowboy Bebop" after I turned into an adult, and that too left an impact on me.

It's no secret I'm influenced by these works, so combining the unlikely worlds of "Gasoline-filled robots working in mundane life" and "Cool and stylish jazz fusion" has been great fun. It's exciting to see what synergy it could create. 

"Shinobi non Grata" was intentionally designed to be a fast-paced 8-bit action game, so we requested our composer to use the old Famicom sound palette to create the background music. (I still believe it has some of the best soundtracks ever.) This time, we don't have to emulate an old gaming console, and our priority lies in choosing music that fits the "90's anime" vibe.

If you're a fan of 90's anime, you'd know what I mean. The objective is to get that "feel" throughout the game. We put in a lot of effort in the graphics for "Shinobi non Grata" and we aren't lowering our standards for this game, either.

Till the next time.

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: Saul Bass and Scramble Vice
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/a9f26ee1e31ef6bd6741a8409922a916d9d82a55.png[/img]
Our previous game "Shinobi non Grata" had three visual key points kept in mind during its design. (1) Using a Nintendo Famicom palette, (2) Brush calligraphy and (3) Silhouettes. To create a concrete design, I thought it would be for the best to decide on a visual keypoint for Scramble Vice too.

While thinking about it, I had the idea to combine elements that are on the polar opposite of what you would expect from a Sci-fi game with robots. (I'd have to admit it's also because a futuristic imagination has never been my strong point.)

That's when I thought of Saul Bass. He's the graphics designer that worked on the title logos for movies such as "Psycho", "The Man with the Golden Arm'', "North by Northwest", "Vertigo", and of course one of my favorite anime, "Cowboy Bebop".  His style of using simple shapes and deformed silhouettes seemed perfect to create a retro look that would give a contrasting edge. Something that would seem contradicting in style, which is what I was looking for.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/65baef636d9dbb28d3ea6749a73a366181d5934f.png[/img]

Once that was decided, it was easier to grasp the tone of the game and what kind of music we should use. Something set in the future, yet feels old. A game where you could vibe with jazz in the background while you blow up villains and Tokyo.

There's a bit of fear wondering how this game would be received, being something that fuses two different styles together. But we're working hard to make something solid, so we hope you'll stick with us.

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: Antiheroes and Scramble Vice
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/358f3dc8b3c939cf985d8a2b441abc55daba795a.png[/img]

Scramble Vice was inspired by the late Mikiya Mochizuki's manga "Wild 7". The idea formed when I began to think it might be interesting to create a robot story with a hero that breaks the rules.

Everything started out light-heartedly, but as I was creating the movie clips it evolved into what it is now: Rule breaking policemen that ride robots, wreak havoc even when there are civilians around, and even think nothing of destroying the city as they take down criminals.

Modern society can lead us to feel trapped, so having a game that allows you the freedom as an antihero that goes a little crazy to get the job done could be fun and liberating. I thought something like that would be appreciated globally. It's what I keep in mind as I write the instruction manuals, work on the dot art and run the test plays.

Storywise, I was influenced by the book "Farewell, my lovely '' by Raymond Chandler. It's a book I read when I was in primary 5, and although I didn't understand it at that time, it got me hooked on mystery novels. Instead of a storyline that deals with large scale wars and revolutions, I wanted to work on crimes that humans commit. Problems that are solved by utilizing robots, but occurring in daily life so it can be relatable enough. That's what will make or break the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/1ec8d0e42ab52b63a76120dd7aa46d05cc850342.png[/img]

It's a robot game essentially, but I want it to feel human. That's why I plan to have the protagonist Sakuragi and her teammates be expressive of their emotions. They need to laugh, get angry, get shocked, dumbfounded, be raw. That sounds completely the opposite of what you would expect from a protagonist of a mystery novel, who's usually calm and collected, but I'm aiming to create a game that can fluctuate easily from something serious to comedic, and vice versa. 

We're in the stage where both enemy and protagonist machines are in motion. We're getting into the meat of things. Hope you stick around to check it out.

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: Animation: 3D movement
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/10c82a7f9ba3b3c5c99af8b23a2db4e73095ec74.png[/img]
There's one thing we've been particular about in the animation for Scramble Vice, and that's to make the characters look and move as if their 3D. Lately, there's a popular tactic using rotation, shrink and expand functions to create layers for 2D animations, but we've made a point not to use those methods as much as possible and create animation patterns instead.

We haven't been drawing the characters straight from the front, or directly from the side. By drawing how they run and walk with their 3D dimensions in mind, they have a more solid presence. Having designated artwork of the characters standing with their legs slightly apart and their feet firmly planted to the ground give a better effect of their weight.

Although it's a robot game, it was also important to make their movements not too stiff… To express their hydraulics for their punches, jumps and landing, we're using more frames than usual. (We do need to keep operability in mind, so the balance is difficult.)

Also, pursuing their three-dimensional movements inevitably leads to having the characters pose stylishly in each frame. One of my favorites is using the roller dash; the crouch, the spike hammered into the ground and swivel like a compass is just so cool.

I could talk about this all day. The enemy robots have their own signature movements and poses to express their character. For example, I think we did great with the builder-bot; it looks a little janky in action. Again, keeping their 3D movement in mind has been crucial in bringing out each robot's uniqueness.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/4bdc5d6aad483da843a95cdb92aa801a1d6aeb24.png[/img]
Progress is going smoothly for the pixel art for the objects. We have a few robots and characters that are important on which we will start. My ambition is to have players of the game think, "Wow, those robots were awesome, what a cool game." We're working on it.

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: Pixel Art: Density
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/77ee0ea60dacf8cd3504e6b56842982b9003af7e.png[/img]
In our previous game Shinobi non grata, the topic was to try and push the limits of 8-bit animation. Because the story has a protagonist left behind the times, it was meaningful to have the graphics look like it was made for a very old game console.

This time however, the game is about combat robots in the future… Having solid, realistic details are essential to make it work. That's why we're putting a lot of effort in the pixel art. One of my favorite games, "In the hunt (1993)", comes to mind as I create the art pixel by pixel so this would become a game that makes destruction fun.

The protagonist's exoskeleton has been redone from scratch. That's how committed we are. Even the enemy robots have several varieties of animations, although their main purpose is to be taken down. I think I mentioned in my previous post how enemies play a big role in world creation, so we're making a point to create their visuals to make them act and look the part of a villain.

As for the pilots and other human characters, they are colored in a cartoonish, simple manner, but we're being careful in their clothing and details. The goal is to make each character come alive in their own skin, so they look the part of a team of misfit police officers. Personally, I'm fond of the undercover agent character "Nanigashi". The "?" drawn on his mask is so silly, I love it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/ca943335e2b187fd580cb6c978a04f40dcdbf336.png[/img]

The pixel art takes 10 times more than Shinobi non grata, but even so, whenever I see the art on screen it makes me want to do more. It's beginning to be a problem.

That's it about the pixel art.

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: About the storyline
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/2f0a20c3ae5c2109ae4b24a2047065cecd4dd488.png[/img]
Shinobi non Grata wasn't meant to be focused heavily on the storytelling, but even so, it was designed to plant a seed of doubt by the last stage through the background, credit visuals and effects. "Was the fight truly about a generational change? Maybe it has a different meaning to it." If you were led to believe so, you might see the game in a different light.

Scramble Vice, on the contrary, has a plotline that develops as you make progress. The main storyline unfolds as you gradually get closer to the truth, you're able to enjoy banter between the protagonist and other team members, and there are sub-missions that are short stories of their own. We're trying to put in effort even in the details apart from the gameplay.

It was difficult to get to know the characters in Shinobi on Grata, since it was a hardcore ninja action game where most characters are killed off quickly. This time, you'll be able to watch the characters grow.

If you're interested in our previous game Shinobi non Grata, check it out here!
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1796870/SHINOBI_NON_GRATA/

"See you Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: Speed and Weight
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/5ba9c6f96838e53905d7da53793a3e2e58b33f70.png[/img]
"Speed" was the principle element in our previous game, "Shinobi non Grata." So, starting from the game design, controls and visuals to music, the game was tuned to unfold at a fast pace. It was made to feel the excitement of running through the battlefield, slashing past hordes of enemies and fighting formidable shinobi bosses... The pace and rhythm of the game is what, I feel, made the game fun.

For "Scramble Vice" I'm hoping to make "weight" the element of fun for the game. By that, I don't mean to simply make the controls feel slow and heavy, but when the robots jump or attack, I want them to react in a way suitable to their weight. When they use their vernier thrusters to dash or when they take flight, I want the controls to feel smooth but tune it in a way you still feel the weight of the machine. That also goes for the sound design; I want the sound to reflect the weight as well.

We designed the stages for "Shinobi non Grata" so there would be variety, and comparably, we're trying to find a range of ways to have fun in "Scramble Vice" too.

If you're interested in "Shinobi non Grata", have a look here:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1796870/SHINOBI_NON_GRATA/

It's a ninja game, but sometimes you'll fight mechanical enemies.

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: Pilot Mode
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/29abe1f6814f9b82ab03a4bed6aa910be21a07a7.png[/img]

We're working hard to create a solid robot action game, but we're also designing missions where the pilot will have to leave her machine behind to fight the enemy crime syndicate. When our protagonist Kei Sakuragi heads out with her handgun to fight terrorists in the flesh, she'll find herself facing tanks and cannons that wouldn't have been formidable had she had her robot with her. Exciting, no?

On the way, she could find a powerful side arm, or maybe take control of a car or motorbike. We're thinking of ways to expand on the variety of fun. If we could make her robot exoskeleton feel like just another vehicle she could ride, that would be great.

Being able to see a tiny character in motion should be fun in itself. Or at least, that what I tell myself while I add little touches to the pixel art we create every day. It's definitely going to be something to look forward to!

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: What Scramble Vice aims to feel like
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/f14bbe339621b84f71815e8aa124cafe15d90a6a.png[/img]

In our previous game "Shinobi non grata", we made 8-bit graphics with sharp contrast for a cleaner look. This time, the dot graphics are made with finer details for higher visual intensity. Destruction is a big part of the fun in this action game, so we've made it a point to make the robots detailed so it's satisfying when they're blown up using explosions and guns.

I have an opinion that in essence; a robot game is fun when you're able to control a heavy machine and make it wreak havoc in the front lines despite getting shot at. I'm constantly thinking of ways to create situations that would make that possible.

Shinobi non grata was created with the idea of beating several types of bosses with speed and style. This time, the gameplay is in maneuvering unique robots that have strong characteristics... I'm hoping to simulate a similar type of excitement to taming a wild horse.

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: Thanks to our localizers.
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/31f923f3b1d5c271f90bf56ad538986a211083d7.png[/img]

After releasing the PV, we've been receiving lots of encouraging messages from around the world. Naturally, that directs my attention to the localization of the game.

When I thought about the title of the game, I was reading an article about the TV drama "Miami Vice". The title in Japanese is translated as "Miami Special Investigation Squad" so I simply thought, "Maybe Vice is a police term in English." But then, I asked our localizer and got the reply that no, the word "Vice" has nothing to do with the meaning squad or investigation...

What does it mean then? "Immoral or wicked behavior, criminal activities." Oh. Sounds too serious and not quite what I was looking for. But then, I also got the explanation that it also means having a moral fault or bad habit you just can't quit. So by combining it with the world "Scramble", meaning to move in urgency or panic in a disorderly fashion, it could imply being hooked on chaos.

So, that's how we got the title for our trigger-happy game. It sits well with me since the game's fun is in enthusiastically blowing things up everywhere. I doubt auto translate could have given me the same satisfaction, so thanks to our localizers!

As you can see, we've got many people working on the project. We'd really appreciate it if you could add us to your wish list...

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: About Enemy Design
notes.notes:
When creating the enemy, I try to be mindful whether the design wouldn't look out of place even when seen repeatedly. What I mean by that is by having some sort of uniform design, or something in common, we can recognize they come from the same organization. Take for example the Stormtroopers from Star Wars… Enemies you see often take on a prominent role in world-building, sometimes even more than the protagonist. Again, there's a lot of trial and error involved to get it right.

In Scramble Vice, the most common enemy robot you'll see and fight is the "ZECT". It's designed to look like the opposite of the protagonist's machine; something that looks evil. (It also feels better to destroy something that looks evil.)
--------------------------------------------------------------
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/3ac1f9fa9e82f6c7ba0296dd800a2ea20ea3e84f.png[/img]
[h3]ZECT[/h3]
Touted as the "Battle suit that changes the tide", the ZECT was widely promoted and made its debut in battle during the Northern conflict. It boasts a real-time link to satellite camera and AI tactical support.

However, the ZECT proved to be problematic causing misfire incidents against civilians and pilot injuries. After an in-depth investigation it came to light that its design went against 13 ethics clauses set by the UN. Because of that the ZECT became one of the most loathed machines among its pilots despite its high firepower, even gaining the nickname "Death's Hound".
After the war, the machines were recalled, but not even half were collected. Rumors say terrorists from the new third world took the majority of working units away.

Which is stronger? "Steel Cat" Asura, or "Death's Hound" ZECT?
--------------------------------------------------------------
That's all for now!

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: Designing the mechanics
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/bcdc2002b21c6d00d69b81d103f1c279674453fe.png[/img]

In the world of Scramble Vice, robot battles are just a part of any oother day. We try to keep things convincing enough so the designs "feel possible"  in real life, but making the robotics work and making the controls feel good are two different things. It's a process of trial and error that has us making adjustments continuously.

Robot games are fun because you get to mobilize a unit that can be tricky in its functions, and run head on into gunfire knowing your armor can take it to some degree. We're trying to get the perfect balance of the robot functions, destruction mechanics and gameplay pacing so Scramble Vice can be an action game that keeps players on their toes.

The theme of the mechanical design is to have "details convincing enough it could be possible in reality." For example, the gangway to the cockpit, the rollers on the heels of the robots (the covers rise whenever the rollers are in use) and muzzle flash on firearms that cast shadows in different angles depending on where the flash occurred. Minute details like that which nobody might notice. Even the rockets on the robot's body are designed to be used for turning and dashing apart from its basic function of flying.

People that love robot games have an eye for detail like that. It isn't something we can overlook. The game itself is still going to be made so everyone can have fun with it, but by paying attention to detail, whenever someone notices it may put a smile on their face. We hope that could be you.

That's all for now.

See you, Scramble Vice!!

notes.notes: [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/08e26499ffe3ae8ab30587c996ab610847ec319b.png[/img]

notes.title: Happy Holidays!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/137d33a1873afa699f196ed8b2720ffd13049d58.png[/img]

It's been a busy and fulfilling year for Studio Pico, with the release of Shinobi non grata out on PC and other platforms and starting the development of Scramble Vice soon after.

I remember thinking hard about how to pitch Scramble Vice to publishers, creating PVs and documents for the presentation and feeling extremely nervous. But after showing just the PV, I got such an easy, chill response of "Okay then, let's make it." That caught me so off guard, it took me a while to have it sink in as all the anxiety left my body in an instant.

After releasing the PV, there has been an overwhelming response. All our staff were surprised to know there are so many fans of 90's anime and video games overseas. It's really encouraging, and we're all revved up to make something good. Just like Shinobi non grata, I want the game to have its fun in the action as its core,  but add in all the things that I love, all the easter eggs I can manage so the game can be enjoyed in multiple ways.

So, we're working hard towards its release next year. We hope you'll stay for the ride, and maybe add the game to your wish list. Have a good new year!

"See you, Scramble Vice!!"

notes.title: The world of Scramble Vice
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/7dc3cebc62049a377e25d94e133241fef8f212ca.png[/img]

In my previous project "Shinobi non grata", I think I was successful in creating a world that portrayed the dark and treacherous path of the ninja… but at the same time, I felt it was hard to feel for the characters since most of them got killed off before you could get to know them. So this time, I wanted the characters to have a chance to express their emotions; have them laugh, get angry, maybe get a little ugly, make some mistakes and grow.

The protagonist Kei Sakuragi grew up in a family that have worked in the police force for generations. She rebelled against her strict upbringing and got involved in a juvenile gang fight, causing her to be charged for battery. This became a turning point for her, and she eventually joined the department where her father, who died in the line of duty 7 years ago, used to work. Now, she fights terrorists with her team, and I hope I can portray her growth as she learns to find her own path.

Kei's story and the showy robot action are the main themes of this game.

I'm working hard on it! Scramble Vice is on the way! If you could add it to your wish list, I'd really appreciate it!!

See you Scramble Vice！

notes.title: Scramble Vice on call!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/d0eeff7e4870522faff43df2e27ee6241ac93257.png[/img]

Hi there! I’m Pikopiko256. 
We’ve started development of our futuristic robot action game “Scramble Vice”, and its store page is finally up and running.

“Scramble Vice” has got robot battles galore, it’s action-packed, its graphics are positively destructive, there’s banter with party members, there’s mystery, style, jazz fusion music - all the good stuff wrapped up in a 90’s style anime aesthetic.

In this column, instead of reporting on development progress, I’d like to talk a bit more about the game and its design.

I hope you’ll stick around!

notes.title: The Scramble Vice Story
notes.notes:
[h2]The Scramble Vice  Story[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/f171854c948ded2736c29c81d2993212922102d9.png[/img]
[u]Chapter 1 “World New Order”[/u]
During construction of a venue to host the 3rd Expo, a wrecking suit has gone berserk on site.
The 9th mobility unit is dispatched immediately, but find the wrecking suit empty once they subdue it.
According to reports the suit went out of control due to an AI malfunction.
Uncoincidentally, a terrorist group who call themselves “World New Order "had announced on web media they would strike at the same time the suit lost control.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/d71c00e1bf316cc9bc12dc5f1a5db4c898052d36.png[/img]
[u]Chapter 2 “Lord of the Flies”[/u]
Several scandals on bigwig politicians and celebrities are being leaked, causing an uproar in Neo Tokyo. An anonymous hacker group has hijacked the city’s security camera and drone system to spy on them, spreading their darkest secrets on the web.
The poster uses the pseudonym“Lord of the Flies”. What is the motive behind all of this?




[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/3100d9a77c89bef311f45c07c2d35fd316e93bed.png[/img]
[u]Chapter 3 “The Great Outcast”[/u]
Robberies centered on mega retro banks and NFT markets have been occurring one after the other. Whats more the stolen money is being sent to charity organizations and the cash trails are being scrubbed clean.
Research uncovers the mastermind might be the very same person who stole an assault suit from the military 3 years ago and used it to rob criminal organizations to donate to charity.
Who is this modern day Robin Hood?




[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/59f138b96c83c2e5eac71f4eb31048588f956def.png[/img]
[u]Chapter 4 “All Living Creatures”[/u]
The team receives an anonymous tip that the terrorist group “World New Order”has a subsidiary running a weapons factory in Yokohama. The 9th mobile unit head out but the enemy is one step ahead of them. The fight expands to involve assault suits scouring the entirety of China Town.
When things can’t seem to get any worse, a giant mobile weapon emerges from a hangar, engulfing the city in flames.

notes.title: The Scramble Vice Main Characters 02
notes.notes:
[h2]The Scramble Vice
Main Characters 02[/h2]

Tidbit 2: A baddass female lead, a straight-laced leader, an incurable playboy, a well-born lady, a shifty old man… the list goes on.
In Shinobi non grata, the protagonist worked alone. But this time there’s a whole bunch of characters with merry banter.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/7054615bf7e414eaa1e79447b6e7356b49d2d154.png[/img]
[u]Mai Ryugasaki[/u]
Heiress of the conglomerate “Ryugasaki Group”, Mai could have lived a cushy life but chose to join the 9th mobile unit so she may contribute to society.
Her family thought she would come running back after having a taste of the rigorous training at the police force, but Mai has become an indispensable communications officer for her unit with her quick wits, calm personality and high social skills.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/608afd7935894c59581a4fbeb2559e55b74adbd3.png[/img]
[u]Asuha Kiryu[/u]
Mechanic of the 9th mobile unit. She stepped in her grandfather’s shoes after he began having difficulties working from rheumatism. She’s terrific at her job, but drinks, gambles, and smokes like there’s no tomorrow. A big fan of the Carps baseball team, she’ll be in a bad mood the day after they lose a match. A good friend of Kei’s, they often hit the bars together.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/2c829fd80caef7edb0c4493134bd2b505aacaa3e.png[/img]
[u]Nanigashi[/u]
An officer with a thousand faces. Originally an undercover agent, he’s destroyed several crime syndicates. He made a grave mistake while working undercover, which caused him to be ostracized from his unit. It was then when Jinguji offered him a position in the Scramble Vice. He’s particularly good at close combat.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/be66a1a503e012224c5b4fb276cbe43f1ccd1460.png[/img]
[u]Asura[/u]
4th generation exoskeletal assault suit used by the 9th mobile unit. Due to budget, it’s a slightly older model, but it is customizable and able to install a wide variety of weapons. It’s hard shell and high mobility earned it’s nickname “Steel Cat”.
Like other suits, a leveled electronic warrant has to be issued for it to be unlocked, but if its AI system deems it relevant Asura is able to open fire without provocation.

notes.title: The Scramble Vice Main Characters 01
notes.notes:
[h2]The Scramble Vice
Main Characters 01[/h2]

Tidbit 1: The 9th mobile unit is notorious for its problematic characters and low sense of propriety despite being in the police force. Whenever they are dispatched, destruction is inevitable, so many members of the metropolitan assembly fear them and consider them the bane of Neo Tokyo’s existence.




[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/540db6d885a0ed0fd4eccd4be24b03c844255e1f.png[/img]
[u]Kei Sakuragi[/u]
Formerly a delinquent that joined the police acadamy because she was promised she could “be as destructive as she wants”. After strict training, she’s reformed(?) and is currently in her third year within the police force. She may be rough around the edges, but her comrades in the Scramble Vice respect and trust her. Her father was also a policeman that died in the line of duty 7 years ago.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/9c77184d172688ecbd552034010ec9db8162e089.png[/img]
[u]Jotaro Jinguji[/u]
Captain of the Scramble Vice (aka the 9th mobile unit.) Despite its problematic members, he manages to keep the team together and lead them to protect Neo Tokyo. Serious and stubborn, he puts his trust in every one of his men unreservedly. He is also the one responsible for reforming Kei, partly because he feels he owes her father having been in his care in the past. Married with two kids, he’s also a doting dad.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/f0ada5564cd4e158e447d98ede549d67189be17b.png[/img]
[u]Cliff Emerson[/u]
Vanguard of the Scramble Vice. A ladies man through and through, even the reason he became a policeman is because “chicks dig heroes”. He looks and behaves like a playboy but has a surprisingly strong sense of justice, and would never leave a damsel in distress. He’s been trying his moves on Kei, who rejects him mercilessly, but never lets that get him down.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44612937/e181c393be59897c109eed29d0bb91cb1ca14974.png[/img]
[u]Professor[/u]
Formally an Assault Suit Driver from Public Security Intelligence. He seems to have a dark past, but hides it will with his chill attitude. He’s helped the 9th mobile unit get out of sticky situations using the dirt he has on politicians several times. Old, but not rusty. He may have a low regard for the law, but he’s as chivalrous as it gets.
